editorial:
Imagine being the kind of guy who does everything right, never lies, and just takes the hits from a mean boss and a demanding fiancé. That is John. He is basically a doormat who is just waiting for his life to finally start. But then Rick Carlson shows up and ruins everything. Rick is the total opposite of John; he is a smooth talker who knows how to manipulate people to get what he wants. He doesn't just move into John's building, he actually lands a job at the same law firm. It feels like a slow-motion car crash as you watch Rick slowly push John out of his own life and take over everything he worked for.

You will probably find yourself yelling at the screen because John is too nice, but that is where the tension comes from. The acting is solid, and the way the power dynamic shifts keeps you interested. While the pacing starts a bit slow, the twists in the second half make it worth it. If you enjoy stories about a nice guy finally hitting a breaking point, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can find a 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection, but renting it on Apple TV is a quick and easy way to watch it tonight.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when John finally stops being a victim and fights back against Rick. He realizes that being the nice guy got him nowhere and uses Rick's own tricks against him. In the final scenes, John manages to outsmart Rick and expose his lies to the firm and his fiancé. Rick loses his power and his status, while John finally finds his backbone and takes control of his own life and career.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological games and underdog stories.
